notes: ACCESS: direct fetch, no blocking, exactly as the prior Home-Decor pass reported. burrow.com is a headless Shopify store on Hydrogen/Oxygen with a Sanity CMS front end (react-router / turbo-stream). TREE: taken from the rendered mega-menu in the homepage HTML (110 data-click-id="main-menu_*" links, giving departments Bestsellers / Seating / Living / Dining / Bedroom / Office / Outdoor / Rugs & Decor / Storage / Warehouse), cross-checked against the SEO link block repeated on every collection page and against both collection sitemaps (sitemap/collections/1.xml + 2.xml = 156 handles). I also opened all eight department landing pages (/seating /living /dining /bedroom /home-office /outdoor /storage /rugs-decor) and diffed their collection links against the menu: the only extras were brand collections (Ember, Field, Mercer, Russet, Union, Dunes, Relay) and /collections/bookcases-shelves, so the mega-menu is the site's full category tree and there is no deeper navigable level. QTY METHOD: Burrow displays NO product count anywhere - no 'N products' header, no 'Showing 1-24 of N'. Confirmed by a rendered read of /collections/bookcases (no count text, 20 tiles, no Load more) which matched my enumeration exactly. There is no Liquid endpoint either (/collections/<h>/products.json and /products.json both 404 - headless), so the Shopify products_count inflation trap does not arise. I therefore used full enumeration (brief method 3): each collection's own react-router loader payload at /collections/<handle>.data?_routes=routes/collections.$handle exposes collection.products.nodes plus pageInfo{hasNextPage,endCursor}; I followed the site's own ?direction=next&cursor= pagination to hasNextPage=false and counted unique gid://shopify/Product ids (never hrefs). Sanity checks: counts vary per category (1 to 213, no constant); every collection terminated with hasNextPage=false; no duplicate ids appeared across pages of any collection; and a second independent read of sofas-sectionals, loveseats, modular-furniture, beds, wall-shelves, shop-all-outdoor-dining and chairs-ottomans returned identical numbers. I deliberately did NOT use the Shopify filter facet counts - on sofas-sectionals the configuration_type facet values sum to 265 against a true 213, so they are multi-valued and inflated. EXCLUDED: Rugs, Performance Rugs, Pillows (textiles); Trays (decor, already captured by the Home-Decor pass); Mattresses and Sleep Kits (bedding); Bar Carts & Trays /collections/carts-trays (3 products = the Dram Bar Cart plus the same Ottoman Tray and Round Tray - not furniture-primary, and its bar cart is already inside Bar Carts & Credenzas, overlap verified = 1); /collections/lighting and /collections/table-lamps (still zero live products); Bestsellers, Warehouse/Clearance and all six clearance-* children, 'In Stock - Ready to Ship' stock filters, 'View All', 'Compare Collections', and the brand collections (Nomad, Range, Shift, Ember, Field, Mercer, Russet, Union, Dunes, Relay, Index, Title, Canon...) - all brief section 3 junk. LANDING PAGES: Seating > 'Sofas' (/sofas) and 'Sectionals' (/sectionals) are Sanity CMS pages served by the catch-all routes/$ route with no collection object and no pageInfo - they are landing pages, not listings, so they are not emitted; the site's own listing for that population is the Living menu's 'Sofas & Sectionals' (/collections/sofas-sectionals, 213), which is recorded. Same for the eight department pages, which appear only as grouping rows. UNNAVIGABLE SUB-COLLECTIONS: the collection sitemap contains finer handles that appear in NO menu and on NO landing page - coffee-tables (5), side-tables (4), accent-tables (8) under Coffee & Side Tables (10); dining-tables-outdoor (6), dining-chairs-outdoor (4), dining-sets-outdoor (3) under Outdoor Dining (11); u-sectionals, chaise-sectionals, corner-sectionals, modular-sectionals under Sofas & Sectionals. I checked each: they are overlapping re-cuts, not a partition (the three table handles union to 9 of the parent's 10; the three outdoor-dining handles sum to 13 but union to 9 of 11), and the site never links them, so I kept the navigable menu leaf rather than inventing a level the site does not have. OVERLAP: Burrow files the same product under several department cuts, so some rows genuinely double-count each other; the three worst cases (Modular Seating, Chairs & Ottomans, Wall Shelves) carry flags with the measured overlaps. Nodes repeated verbatim across menus (Sleeper Sofas in Seating/Living/Bedroom/Office, Bookcases in Living/Office/Storage, Credenzas & Media Storage in Living/Office/Storage, Coffee & Side Tables in Living/Storage) are emitted once, under their first department.
